Project brief

Memory Museum explores how human memory has evolved alongside cultural and technological development. Beginning with Matteo Ricci’s Memory Palace and Bernard Stiegler’s theory of primary, secondary, and tertiary memory, the project translates different modes of remembering into architectural experiences. Three interconnected programmes—a government meeting space, a religious space, and an archaeological research institute—correspond respectively to immediate memory, long-term personal memory, and technologically externalised memory. Through overlapping programmes, shifting thresholds, material transitions, light, and different forms of exhibition, these abstract processes of memory are transformed into a continuous spatial narrative. Rather than treating memory as something contained solely within the mind, the museum traces its transformation from immediate perception and personal recollection to externalised technological storage. Designed as an expandable structure extending towards the Meiguan Ancient Road, the architecture itself grows and accumulates over time, echoing the evolving nature of human memory.
